title: Your playbook
teaches: A playbook is your own written set of best plays: after each session you write up the setup that made the most sense, section by section (the market, the catalyst, the chart, how buyers and sellers acted, and how you managed it), you start with a few plays you know well, and you fit the format to how you trade.

sources.title: The PlayBook: An Inside Look at How to Think Like a Professional Trader (Mike Bellafiore; first printing July 2013): the publisher's sample pages (contents, introduction, index)
sources.why_reliable: The book itself as published: the publisher's own sample pages on Pearson's media server (copyright page: Publishing as FT Press, First Printing July 2013, ISBN 978-0-13-293764-1). Bellafiore co-founded SMB Capital, a New York proprietary trading firm, and the unit plan names this book's PlayBook method as the source. Quoted only as his method.

facts.quote: After each trading session, I ask the players on our desk (and now you?) to archive a trading setup that made the most sense to them during that day.
facts.claim: Bellafiore has his traders write up, after every session, the setup that made the most sense to them that day.

facts.quote: They archive this play in a template form, which we share: the SMB PlayBook.
facts.claim: The play is written up on a fixed template, and the collected pages are the SMB PlayBook.

facts.quote: This exercise brands their winning trades in their trading brain, synthesizes the most important market patterns for them to study, and helps them internalize their best trading setups so that they trade them instinctively in real-time.
facts.claim: Writing the play up helps a trader internalize it, so they trade it instinctively when it shows up again.

facts.quote: We break down each trade as follows: The Big Picture Intraday Fundamentals Technical Analysis Reading the Tape Trade Management Trade Strategy Trade Review
facts.claim: The book's PlayBook sections: big picture, intraday fundamentals, technical analysis, tape reading, trade management, trade strategy, trade review.

facts.quote: It is not my intention to preach that you should dissect trades exactly like I do, as you may trade a different product or time frame
facts.claim: Bellafiore does not ask you to copy his sections exactly, since you may trade a different product or time frame.

facts.quote: I do, however, encourage you to develop a similar system of archiving your best trading setups that makes the most sense to you in the format that works best for you.
facts.claim: Build your own system for archiving your best setups, in the format that works for you.

facts.quote: Your PlayBook’s contents are up to you. But its existence, with all due respect, should not be.
facts.claim: What goes in your playbook is your choice; having one is not optional.

facts.quote: Recently, I met with a series of very experienced but underperforming traders.
facts.claim: Bellafiore met a group of very experienced traders who were underperforming.

facts.quote: The common denominator for this group was that none of them had a methodology to archive their favorite setups, nor could they clearly, definitively, and instantly articulate their best plays.
facts.claim: What they shared: no method to archive their favorite setups, and no clear, instant way to say what their best plays were.

facts.quote: Focus unrelentingly on what setups make the most sense to you.
facts.claim: Focus hard on the setups that make the most sense to you.

facts.quote: You do not become a great trader by being shown cookie cutter technical setups and then soon become successful.
facts.claim: Being shown ready-made setups does not make you a great trader.

facts.quote: Trades will stop working, and you will have to find new ones that do work.
facts.claim: Plays can stop working over time, and then you find new ones.

facts.quote: Then you can execute these plays as automatically as you breathe, walk, and talk. But before, each trade is a struggle of indecision and uncertainty.
facts.claim: Once a play is internalized you execute it automatically; before that, each trade is a struggle of indecision.

facts.quote: They spend their energy searching for more of their favorite setups and focus on where they can add size responsibly.
facts.claim: The best traders look for more of their favorite setups and add size responsibly.

facts.quote: We review his failed trade in JCP that was still One Good Trade.
facts.claim: The book reviews a losing JCP trade that was still a good trade.

facts.quote: The Big Picture: First Know What Is Moving the Market
facts.claim: The big picture section comes first: know what is moving the market.

facts.quote: Intraday Fundamentals: Trade with Real Order Flow Behind Your Stocks
facts.claim: The intraday fundamentals section is about the real buying and selling a stock's news brings in.

facts.quote: Reading the Tape: Find Better Entries and Exits
facts.claim: Tape reading, watching the actual orders, is there to find better entries and exits.

facts.quote: You are only as good as the stocks you trade.
facts.claim: Your results are only as good as the stocks you pick to trade.

facts.quote: You Are Trading Too Many Stocks
facts.claim: A section of the book is titled You Are Trading Too Many Stocks.

facts.quote: We ask our traders to create a playbook. Plays and patterns that make sense to them that they want to trade more of.
facts.claim: A playbook is the plays and patterns that make sense to you and that you want to trade more of.

facts.quote: At the end of the day the trader considers a best trade they made, details this trade in our SMB PlayBook template form and then sends it to me.
facts.claim: At the end of each day the trader writes up a best trade on the PlayBook form and sends it to Bellafiore.

facts.quote: Name of The Play: Gap and Go Above LT Level w/ Buyer
facts.claim: The form starts with a short name for the play.

facts.quote: Intraday Fundamentals: Sysco beats by $0.03, beats on revs
facts.claim: In the SYY entry, the earnings and revenue beat is written under intraday fundamentals.

facts.quote: Technical Analysis: 30.50, 31.50, and 32 were longer term technical levels.
facts.claim: In the SYY entry, the chart's price levels are written under technical analysis.

facts.quote: Reading the Tape: There was a clear buyer at 30.63
facts.claim: In the SYY entry, a big buyer holding one price is written under tape reading.

facts.quote: All traders can review this playbook and get some practice on specific trades or co-opt one of these trades for themselves.
facts.claim: The shared playbook lets traders practise on each other's plays and adopt one for themselves.

facts.quote: In The PlayBook, my thesis was for traders to study their best trades and build from them, trading these setups more often and bigger.
facts.claim: Bellafiore's thesis: study your best trades, build from them, and trade those setups more often and bigger.

facts.quote: If you are not actively studying your strengths, consider doing so.
facts.claim: Study your strengths on purpose.

facts.quote: SMB coined the term “intraday fundamentals”. It refers to the study of news patterns that provide us clues to how a stock may move intraday.
facts.claim: Intraday fundamentals means the news behind a stock and the clues it gives about how the stock may move.

facts.quote: We find a stock that has had fresh news of late, so a catalyst behind it. We look for the technicals, long and short, to align.
facts.claim: SMB's longer trades start with a stock with fresh news, a catalyst, and then technicals that line up.

facts.quote: When I make a trading decision I do not just Read the Tape.  When deciding to buy or sell I do not just consult my charts.
facts.claim: Bellafiore never decides on the order flow alone or the chart alone.

facts.quote: For a basketball or football team, a playbook is a set of plays that the team runs in various situations.
facts.claim: A team's playbook is the set of plays it runs in different situations.

facts.quote: Much of the skill of a coach is knowing which plays to call when.
facts.claim: Much of the skill is knowing which play fits which situation.

facts.quote: Successful traders, I find, start with small, focused playbooks and work at becoming proficient in just a few types of trades.
facts.claim: In Steenbarger's experience, good traders start with a small, focused playbook of a few types of trades.

facts.quote: They document their plays in journals, trade them in real time, and review action at the end of the day to see what they might have missed.
facts.claim: They write their plays down, trade them, and review at the end of the day.

facts.quote: Only when they become proficient at a few basic plays do they move on to exploit other ways of making money.
facts.claim: They add new plays only after they are proficient at the first few.

facts.quote: It's common among active traders to think of playbook trades as "setups", as in chart patterns, but this is shortsighted.
facts.claim: Treating a playbook trade as just a chart pattern is shortsighted.

facts.quote: A pattern of market behavior that has led to favorable market returns over a defined time horizon;
facts.claim: A playbook trade starts with a pattern of market behavior that has paid over a defined time frame.

facts.quote: A set of rules for identifying this pattern in real time and entering the trade at a point that provides favorable reward relative to risk;
facts.claim: It has rules for spotting the pattern live and entering where reward is good relative to risk.

facts.quote: A set of rules for sizing the trade, so that the trader can achieve meaningful returns without running the risk of ruin when, by chance, a series of losing trades occurs;
facts.claim: It has sizing rules so a run of losing trades, which comes by chance, cannot ruin you.

facts.quote: A set of rules for establishing target prices and adding to positions/scaling out of positions/exiting positions;
facts.claim: It has rules for targets, adding, scaling out and exiting.

facts.quote: A set of rules for establishing the stocks or instruments best able to exploit the patterns being traded.
facts.claim: It has rules for which stocks suit the pattern best.

facts.quote: When the trader merely views the playbook trade as a set of entry criteria, they leave themselves no guidance for sizing the trade and managing the risk/reward of the position.
facts.claim: A play written as entry rules only gives no guide for sizing or managing the trade.

facts.quote: How trades are sized and managed is every bit as important as the trade ideas themselves
facts.claim: Sizing and managing a trade matter as much as the idea.

facts.quote: the most successful traders are those that find the best vehicles for trading their playbooks
facts.claim: Finding the best stocks to run your plays in is a big part of doing well.

facts.quote: Had they traded exactly the same patterns in the large cap universe, they would have made far less money.
facts.claim: The same patterns made far less money in large caps than in the stocks those traders chose.

facts.quote: What you add is the review and practice that helps make those patterns and rules your own.
facts.claim: Your own review and practice is what makes someone else's patterns and rules yours.

facts.quote: We develop expertise by internalizing what we learn.
facts.claim: Expertise comes from internalizing what you learn.

facts.quote: When I ask traders to identify their strengths, they inevitably give generalized responses that don't map onto best processes.
facts.claim: Asked for their strengths, traders give vague answers that don't map onto a specific process.

facts.quote: it is vital for traders to understand their strengths and how those strengths manifest themselves as successes.
facts.claim: Know your strengths and how they show up in your winning trades.

facts.quote: What was your best trade this year? And what tools/insights/approaches/indicators/charts helped you identify that winning trade?
facts.claim: Review your best trade by asking what helped you find it.

facts.quote: You shouldn't alter a trading plan as a knee-jerk reaction to temporary market events, like when stock prices take a dive.
facts.claim: Don't change your plan as a knee-jerk reaction to short-term market moves.

facts.quote: You may wish to change your trading plan over time.
facts.claim: A plan can change over time, on purpose.

facts.quote: We still concentrate on longer intraday swing trades
facts.claim: Bellafiore's desk trades intraday, mostly longer intraday swing trades.

facts.quote: I would rather have Entry, Stop, Trim, Trail, Advance
facts.claim: We break down each trade we teach as Entry, Stop, Trim, Trail, Advance.

facts.quote: The first trim: the hard rule is a third at 3R; ideally anywhere from 3R to 6R, and in practice he mostly waits for 5R.
facts.claim: Our first trim, the hard rule: a third of the position at 3R. In practice the owner often waits for 5R.

facts.quote: After the first third at 3R: another third at 5R, then trail the last third; adjustable.
facts.claim: After the first third at 3R, we sell another third at 5R and trail the last third.

facts.quote: over the red day's high, on the Kicker day, at market as it trades through
facts.claim: Our Kicker entry is over the red day's high, on the Kicker day, at market as it trades through.

facts.quote: under the Kicker's low, or 3.5% under the entry if that is closer
facts.claim: Our Kicker stop is under the Kicker's low, or 3.5% under the entry if that is closer.

facts.quote: under each higher low, or under the 10-day average
facts.claim: Our Kicker trail is under each higher low, or under the 10-day average.

facts.quote: Hold your winners by selling partials into strength and trailing the rising moving averages.
facts.claim: Our rule: hold winners by selling partials into strength and trailing the rising moving averages.

walkthroughs.title: Your plays, written down
steps: Your playbook is your set of plays, like a team's: setups that make sense to you and that you want more of.
At SMB Capital, Mike Bellafiore's traders write one up after each session: the setup that made the most sense.
The writing is the practice. It helps you act when the play shows up again, instead of hesitating.

walkthroughs.title: One page, section by section
steps: His desk's form opens with a short name for the play. Then come the sections.
His book breaks each trade down in order: big picture, intraday fundamentals, technical analysis, tape reading, trade management, trade strategy, trade review.
In the SYY page he shared, the earnings beat sits under intraday fundamentals. The price levels sit under technical analysis.
A pattern is only part of a play. Trading coach Brett Steenbarger adds sizing, targets, adds and exits.

walkthroughs.title: Make it yours: our Kicker page
steps: Bellafiore trades intraday and says you may trade a different time frame. Build the page in a format that works for you.
Kicker entry: over the red day's high, at market. Stop: under the Kicker candle's low, or 3.5% under entry if closer.
Trims: a third at 3R, a third at 5R. Trail under each higher low or the 10-day average. That's the page.

questions.q: What is a trading playbook?
choices: Your written set of best plays
A list of hot stock tips
A log of every trade you make
Chart patterns from a textbook
questions.answer: Your written set of best plays
questions.why: Your written set of best plays. Bellafiore's traders build it from the plays and patterns that make sense to them and that they want to trade more of. Like a team's playbook, it's the plays you run.
questions.lesson_line: A playbook is your plays, written down. Not tips, not every trade.

wrong.A list of hot stock tips: A tip is a name, not a play. A playbook holds setups you can spot and run again.
wrong.A log of every trade you make: That's your journal. The playbook keeps the setups that made the most sense to you.
wrong.Chart patterns from a textbook: Bellafiore says cookie cutter setups don't make a great trader. The plays have to make sense to you.

questions.q: Bellafiore has his traders write up one play after every trading session.
questions.why: True. After each session, his traders archive the setup that made the most sense to them that day, on the PlayBook form.
questions.lesson_line: One play, written up, every session.

questions.q: Bellafiore breaks each archived trade into sections. Which of these is one of them?
choices: Trade management
Analyst price targets
Your monthly profit goal
What people posted online
questions.why: Trade management. His sections run from the big picture through intraday fundamentals, technical analysis and tape reading to trade management, strategy and review. Steenbarger agrees: targets, adds and exits belong in a play.
questions.lesson_line: A play isn't only the entry. How you manage it is part of the page.

wrong.Analyst price targets: Not one of his sections. The page covers the market, the stock's news, its chart and how you traded it.
wrong.Your monthly profit goal: The page records one play. A money goal says nothing about how to spot or run it.
wrong.What people posted online: Not a section. His catalyst section, intraday fundamentals, is the news itself.

questions.q: Finish Bellafiore's rule for the nightly write-up.
questions.sentence: After each session, archive the setup that made the most ___ that day.
questions.why: Sense. Bellafiore asks for the setup that made the most sense to you that day. His desk builds the playbook from plays that make sense to them and that they want more of.
questions.lesson_line: Write up the setup that made the most sense to you, the play you want more of.

questions.q: A playbook page is complete once it describes the chart pattern.
questions.why: False. Steenbarger calls it shortsighted to treat a playbook trade as a chart setup. Written as entry rules only, it gives you no guide for sizing or managing the trade.
questions.lesson_line: Pattern, entry, size, exits. A page needs all of them.

questions.q: Bellafiore wants the play written up the same day. What does the writing do for you?
choices: Helps you act on it without pause
Proves the setup will win next time
Tells you what to buy tomorrow
questions.answer: Helps you act on it without pause
questions.why: It helps you act without hesitating. The write-up helps you internalize the setup so you trade it instinctively. Before that, Bellafiore says, each trade is a struggle of indecision.
questions.lesson_line: Write it down so next time you act instead of debate.

wrong.Proves the setup will win next time: Nothing does that. Steenbarger notes a run of losing trades can come by chance, even in a good play.
wrong.Tells you what to buy tomorrow: It names no stock. It records a play, so you spot it and act when it shows up again.

questions.q: Bellafiore's book starts each trade breakdown with the big picture. What does that section look at?
choices: What is moving the whole market
Why this one stock is moving
Where your stop goes on the trade
questions.answer: What is moving the whole market
questions.why: What is moving the whole market. His book puts it plainly: first know what is moving the market. Plays suit some situations more than others, and Steenbarger says much of the skill is knowing which play to call when.
questions.lesson_line: Start with the market, then the stock, then the trade.

wrong.Why this one stock is moving: That's the next section, intraday fundamentals: the news behind the stock.
wrong.Where your stop goes on the trade: That's trade management, further down the page.

questions.q: The SYY page Bellafiore shared reads: "Sysco beats by $0.03, beats on revs." Which section is that line in?
choices: Intraday fundamentals
Technical analysis
Trade management
Tape reading
questions.why: Intraday fundamentals. That's the news behind the stock, an earnings and revenue beat. SMB's term means the news that gives clues to how a stock may move.
questions.lesson_line: The catalyst goes under intraday fundamentals.

wrong.Technical analysis: His technical section held price levels: 30.50, 31.50 and 32.
wrong.Trade management: That section is how the position was handled, not why the stock moved.
wrong.Tape reading: That section held the order flow: a clear buyer at 30.63.

questions.story: You're writing up today's best trade. The stock beat earnings, gapped up and cleared its 52-week high. You sold half near the close.
questions.q: Which detail goes under technical analysis?
choices: It cleared its 52-week high
It beat earnings estimates
You sold half near the close
questions.why: It cleared its 52-week high. That's a price level on the chart, like the technical levels in Bellafiore's SYY page.
questions.lesson_line: Chart levels go under technical analysis. The news and your exits each get their own box.

wrong.It beat earnings estimates: That's the catalyst. Bellafiore files news like that under intraday fundamentals.
wrong.You sold half near the close: That's how you handled the position: trade management.

questions.q: This is how we break down each trade we teach. Fill in the missing word.
questions.why: Trail. We break each trade we teach into Entry, Stop, Trim, Trail and Advance. Our rule for winners: sell partials into strength and trail the rising moving averages.
questions.lesson_line: Entry, Stop, Trim, Trail, Advance. That's how we break down every trade we teach.

questions.q: Your Kicker page: entry $20.00, stop $19.30. Our first trim is a third at 3R. At what price is it?
questions.why: $22.10. Three times the entry-to-stop risk, added to the $20.00 entry. A third of the position comes off there.
questions.lesson_line: Write the trim prices on the page in dollars, not just as 3R and 5R.

questions.q: You're starting your playbook. How many setups should it hold at first?
choices: A few you know well
Every pattern you can find
One for every stock you watch
questions.why: A few you know well. Steenbarger sees good traders start with small, focused playbooks and add plays only once they're proficient. Bellafiore says the same: focus on the setups that make the most sense to you.
questions.lesson_line: Start with a few plays you know cold. Add more only when those are second nature.

wrong.Every pattern you can find: That spreads you thin. Proficiency comes from a few types of trades first.
wrong.One for every stock you watch: A play is a pattern you run across stocks, with rules for which stocks suit it. It isn't one page per name.

questions.q: The same play can pay very differently depending on which stocks you trade it in.
questions.why: True. Steenbarger saw traders do very well with their patterns in one group of stocks. In large caps, the same patterns would have made far less. Bellafiore: you are only as good as the stocks you trade.
questions.lesson_line: Write down which stocks the play works best in. It's part of the page.

questions.story: Three trades today. A was a big winner on a tip from a friend. B was a small winner on your own setup, traded as written. C lost after you moved your stop lower.
questions.q: Which one goes in your playbook tonight?
choices: B, the setup traded as written
A, the biggest winner
C, so you can learn from it
All three, every trade counts
questions.answer: B, the setup traded as written
questions.why: B. The playbook keeps the setup that made the most sense, a play you want to trade more of. The size of the win isn't the test.
questions.lesson_line: Archive the play you'd gladly run again, not the trade that paid the most.

wrong.A, the biggest winner: A tip isn't a play. A playbook trade starts with a pattern you can spot again.
wrong.C, so you can learn from it: Learn from it in your journal. A trade where you broke your plan isn't a play you want more of.
wrong.All three, every trade counts: That's a trade log. The playbook holds the setups that made the most sense.

questions.q: A trade that lost money can still be a good trade.
questions.why: True. Bellafiore's book reviews a failed JCP trade that was still, in his words, One Good Trade. A play run right still loses sometimes, and Steenbarger notes losing streaks come by chance.
questions.lesson_line: Judge the play by how you ran it, not by one result.

questions.story: You swing trade from daily charts. Bellafiore built his page for intraday trading, with a section on reading live orders.
questions.q: How do you use his template?
choices: Adapt it to your time frame
Copy every section as written
Wait until you day trade
Keep only the chart section
questions.answer: Adapt it to your time frame
questions.why: Adapt it to your time frame. Bellafiore says he doesn't mean for you to dissect trades exactly like him, since you may trade a different time frame. Use the format that works for you.
questions.lesson_line: Keep his idea. Fit the boxes to how you trade.

wrong.Copy every section as written: He says the opposite: you may trade a different product or time frame, so build your own format.
wrong.Wait until you day trade: His line: what goes in your PlayBook is up to you, but having one isn't optional.
wrong.Keep only the chart section: A pattern alone gives you no guide for sizing or managing the trade. Keep those parts, in your terms.

questions.story: Your Gap Support page has worked for months. This week it lost twice, both times at the planned stop.
questions.q: What do you do with the page?
choices: Keep it; judge it over more trades
Tear the page out today
Double size to win it back
Move the stop lower next time
questions.answer: Keep it; judge it over more trades
questions.why: Keep it and judge it over more trades. Two losses at the planned stop can be chance. Fidelity warns against changing a plan as a knee-jerk reaction to short-term moves.
questions.lesson_line: A page earns a rewrite over many trades, not one bad week.

wrong.Tear the page out today: Losing streaks come by chance, and sizing rules plan for them. Plays do stop working, but that shows over many trades.
wrong.Double size to win it back: That's chasing losses. Steenbarger's sizing rules exist so a losing streak can't ruin you.
wrong.Move the stop lower next time: That widens your risk because of one bad week. A knee-jerk change to the plan is what Fidelity warns against.

questions.q: Bellafiore met very experienced traders who were underperforming. What did they have in common?
choices: No method to save their best plays
Too little time watching screens
Too few stocks to choose from
Not enough chart indicators to use
questions.answer: No method to save their best plays
questions.why: No method to archive their best plays. They couldn't clearly and instantly say what their best plays were. Steenbarger hears the same: traders describe their strengths in vague terms that don't map onto a process.
questions.lesson_line: If you can't name your best play in one line, write it down.

wrong.Too little time watching screens: They were very experienced. Time wasn't the gap; the missing method was.
wrong.Too few stocks to choose from: If anything, his book has a section titled You Are Trading Too Many Stocks.
wrong.Not enough chart indicators to use: His common thread was no record of their best plays, not a missing tool.

questions.story: Your Kicker page has worked for months, traded as written. Bellafiore's thesis is to trade your best setups more often and bigger.
questions.q: How do you get bigger?
choices: Step size up inside your risk rules
Double it on the next trade
Drop the stop since it works
Go big after a losing day
questions.answer: Step size up inside your risk rules
questions.why: Step size up inside your risk rules. Bellafiore's best traders add size responsibly. Steenbarger's sizing rules exist so a run of losers, which comes by chance, can't ruin you.
questions.lesson_line: Bigger in your best play, yes. Never bigger than your risk rules allow.

wrong.Double it on the next trade: The next trade can be the first of a losing streak. Size so a streak can't ruin you.
wrong.Drop the stop since it works: A play that works still loses sometimes. The stop is part of the page.
wrong.Go big after a losing day: That's sizing on emotion, not on the play. Responsible size comes from your rules.

questions.story: Your first page is a gap play. It has the play's name, why the stock gapped and the gap levels on the chart. It ends at your entry price.
questions.q: What does the page still need?
choices: Your stop, size and exits
More indicators on the chart
The company's full financials
Nothing, it's ready to trade
questions.why: Your stop, size and exits. A play that ends at the entry gives no guide for sizing or managing the trade. Steenbarger's playbook trade carries rules for sizing, targets, adds and exits.
questions.lesson_line: The page isn't done at the entry. Stop, size and exits finish it.

wrong.More indicators on the chart: The chart part is done. What's missing is how you'll manage the trade.
wrong.The company's full financials: The page already says why it gapped. The catalyst box is covered.
